I have been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years, and my husband and I know every patch of this land. We grow wheat in winter and maize in summer — that is what the soil and climate here are made for, and it is what every household in our village does. I only went to primary school, but I learned farming from my parents and from watching the fields year after year.

For this year, I will plant my winter wheat on all 8 mu in early October. I will buy improved wheat seed — I have done well with varieties like Luyuan 502 in recent years. Before sowing, I will run the rotary tiller to prepare the ground. I will spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal, and then topdress with urea twice: once before winter dormancy and again at green-up in spring. That gives the wheat enough nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. I will irrigate three times using our well pump — before winter, in spring when growth resumes, and once at heading — because rainfall alone is never enough here. I will spray herbicide once early, and then spray two more times for insects and rust, which I have learned not to ignore after losing yield to rust years ago. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant summer maize on the same 8 mu. I will use hybrid seed, probably Denghai 605 — it is what the supply shop recommends and what my neighbors plant. I will not till the soil for maize; there is no time between wheat harvest and maize sowing, and no-tillage saves us labor and fuel. I will apply about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and topdress once with urea later. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat. I will irrigate twice if July turns dry, using our well. I will spray herbicide once after emergence, and spray twice more for stem borers and other pests. I expect about 550 kg per mu from the maize.

At our age, with just the two of us, we keep things simple and practical. We do what has worked for decades, buy our inputs from the local shop, and follow the same calendar as our neighbors.
